body:
The diagram below shows how yoghurt is produced in a dairy, from fresh milk to the finished product.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: The production of yoghurt in a dairy
steps: Fresh milk is heated to about 85°C to kill harmful bacteria
The heated milk is cooled to around 43°C
Live bacterial cultures are added to the milk
The mixture is kept warm for several hours while it ferments
Lactic acid forms and the milk thickens into yoghurt
The yoghurt is cooled rapidly to stop fermentation
Fruit, flavourings or sweeteners may be stirred in
The yoghurt is packed into containers and stored chilled

body:
The diagram below shows the process of making hard cheese in a dairy, including what happens to cheeses that fail inspection.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: The production of hard cheese
steps: Raw milk is pasteurised or heated gently
Starter cultures and rennet are added to the milk
The milk is left until it forms a firm curd
The curd is cut into small pieces
Whey is drained away from the curd
The curds are heated and stirred to remove more whey
The curds are pressed into moulds to form a block
The cheese is salted in brine or by hand
The cheese is left to mature in a cool store for several months
Cheeses that fail inspection are grated for processed cheese
Mature cheeses are cut, wrapped and sent to shops

body:
The diagram below shows the life cycle of a ladybird, including the stages that take place over winter.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: The life cycle of a ladybird
steps: Adult females lay clusters of yellow eggs on leaves near aphids
The eggs hatch into larvae after about four days
Larvae moult several times as they grow
Larvae feed on large numbers of aphids
The mature larva attaches itself to a leaf
The larva sheds its skin to form a pupa
The adult beetle emerges from the pupa after about a week
Adults feed on aphids through the summer months
Some adults lay a second batch of eggs before winter
Remaining adults shelter in leaf litter to hibernate
Hibernating adults wake in spring and breed again

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A town's outdoor food market, present and planned layouts

before.label: Now
features: Market stalls in the station car park, north of the high street
Fruit and vegetable stalls along the northern edge of the car park
Fishmonger and butcher in a covered hall at the west end of the car park
Coffee kiosk at the car park entrance from the high street
Flower stall in the south-east corner of the car park
Bus station south of the high street, backing onto the river
Library on the high street, west of the bus station
Public toilets in the car park, next to the covered hall
Narrow footpath along the river bank behind the bus station

after.label: Planned
features: Market moved to the site of the bus station, south of the high street
Fruit and vegetable stalls arranged around a central square on the former bus station site
Fishmonger and butcher in a new covered hall on the west side of the square
Old covered hall in the station car park converted into an indoor food hall
Station car park returned to parking, with ten spaces kept for stallholders
Coffee kiosk replaced by a row of food stalls along the river bank, south of the square
Flower stall removed altogether
Library unchanged on the high street, west of the square
New public toilets beside the library, at the west entrance to the square
Riverside footpath behind the square widened into a promenade with benches
Cycle racks at the high street entrance to the square
